Description
Team DP NOVA is a 5-member engineering team from Velalar College of Engineering and Technology (VCET), Erode. We are participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge under the track "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data." Our project, AgriShift, processes NASA soil moisture, temperature, and precipitation data to deliver actionable micro-climate advisory for local farmers. Our team is fully formed and currently locking in registration.
summary:
Smart Krishi is a smart farming platform that combines satellite-based climate insights with crop advisory and water-management support. Farmers can select their location, understand local climate conditions, explore suitable crops based on soil and seasonal factors, and make informed irrigation decisions. By making environmental information easier to understand, Smart Krishi aims to support sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.
One-line tagline
“Smart Krishi – Turning Climate Data into Smarter Farming Decisions.”

Project Details – SMART KRISHI

Project Title: Smart Krishi – Climate-Smart Agriculture and Farming Assistance Platform

Smart Krishi is a web-based smart agriculture platform designed to help farmers make better farming decisions using climate information, weather monitoring, crop recommendations, water management, and satellite-based location monitoring.

The main objective of this project is to support farmers in adapting to changing climate conditions, improving agricultural productivity, reducing water wastage, and promoting sustainable farming practices.

1. How Does the Project Work?

Smart Krishi provides four major solutions:

- Climate Insights: Provides weather information such as temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed, and solar radiation based on the selected farm location. It also displays recent climate history and weather-based farming alerts.

- Smart Crop Recommendation: Recommends suitable crops based on the farming season, soil type, and water availability. It helps farmers select crops that are more suitable for their agricultural conditions.

- Smart Water Management: Uses rainfall and temperature information to provide irrigation guidance and help farmers make better water-management decisions.

- Satellite Monitoring: Allows farmers to search for their farm locations and explore satellite imagery and street maps. It also supports device-based location access.

2. Benefits of the Project

- Helps farmers make informed agricultural decisions.

- Reduces unnecessary water consumption through better irrigation planning.

- Supports suitable crop selection based on soil, season, and water availability.

- Provides weather-based alerts to help farmers prepare for changing conditions.

- Helps farmers explore their farmland using satellite maps.

- Promotes sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.

- Makes useful agricultural information accessible through a simple website.

3. Intended Impact of the Project

The intended impact of Smart Krishi is to create a smarter and more sustainable agricultural environment. It aims to reduce climate-related farming risks, improve resource management, encourage efficient irrigation, and support farmers in making data-informed decisions.

The project focuses on helping small-scale and local farmers access useful farming information through a user-friendly digital platform. In the long term, Smart Krishi aims to contribute to better agricultural productivity, water conservation, and climate resilience.

4. Tools, Programming Languages, and Technologies Used

The project was developed using the following technologies:

- HTML5: To create the structure and content of the website.

- CSS3: To design an attractive, responsive, and user-friendly interface.

- JavaScript: To implement interactive features, weather data processing, crop recommendations, and location-based functionality.

- Open-Meteo API: To retrieve current weather conditions, historical weather information, and forecast data.

- Leaflet.js: To create interactive maps.

- Esri World Imagery: To display satellite imagery.

- OpenStreetMap: To provide street maps and map-related information.

- Nominatim API: To search for villages, towns, and farm locations.

- GitHub Pages: To host and publish the project online.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The creativity of Smart Krishi lies in combining multiple agricultural support features into one platform. Instead of requiring farmers to visit different websites for weather information, crop suggestions, water guidance, and satellite maps, Smart Krishi brings these features together in a single interface.

Its location-based climate dashboard, season-and-soil-based crop recommendation system, weather-based farming alerts, and interactive satellite map make it a useful digital solution for modern agriculture.

6. Factors Considered by Our Team

While developing Smart Krishi, our team considered the following factors:

- Farmers' accessibility to digital technology.

- Simplicity and ease of use of the website.

- Local weather and climatic conditions.

- Different soil types and farming seasons.

- Availability of water resources.

- Accuracy and reliability of weather information.

- Sustainable farming practices.

- Environmental protection and climate change adaptation.

- Mobile-friendly and accessible design.

Conclusion

Smart Krishi is an innovative step towards digital and climate-smart agriculture. By combining weather monitoring, crop recommendations, water-management guidance, and satellite mapping, the project aims to empower farmers with useful information and encourage smarter, more sustainable farming for a better tomorrow.
